China Open Source Daily — 2026-08-28 🏛️ State Council Information Office Press Conference (August 26, 2026) — MIIT’s Liu Yulin Frames Open Source as a Three-Pillar Industrial-System Instrument, and Announces OpenHarmony at 1.35 Billion Devices as the World’s Third-Largest Mobile OS 1. CCTV / State Council Information Office (SCIO) — 8月26日 “开局起步’十五五’” series press conference, MIIT Information-Communication-Development Department Director Liu Yulin (刘郁林); headline “强供给 促应用 育生态 多维度发力乘势而上用好新一代信息技术” (Strengthen Supply, Promote Application, Cultivate Ecosystem — Multi-Dimensional Mobilization to Leverage New-Generation Information Technology), republished on 央视网 (CCTV News) and 开放原子开源基金会 (OpenAtom Foundation), 2026-08-26.
On August 26, 2026, the State Council Information Office (国务院新闻办公室 / SCIO) hosted its “开局起步’十五五’” (Launch-of-the-15th-Five-Year-Plan) thematic press-conference series. The MIIT information-communication-development director 刘郁林 (Liu Yulin) delivered three institutional announcements in one session:
(a) The “Strong-Supply / Promote-Application / Cultivate-Ecosystem” three-pillar open-source strategy — 强供给 / 促应用 / 育生态. Liu Yulin framed China’s open-source program for the 15th Five-Year Plan period as a three-pillar industrial-system instrument: strong supply (加大研发投入, 创新组织方式 — increased R&D investment, new organizational modes, concentrated attacks on key technologies; 实施工业数据筑基行动 — industrial-data foundation action; 深入推进"人工智能+软件"行动 — deepening AI-plus-software action), promote application (鼓励各行各业大胆开放应用场景 — encourage all sectors to open application scenarios; 从"用软件"向"享服务"转变 — transition from “using software” to “enjoying services”), and cultivate ecosystem (鼓励开源社区和企业深化开放合作, 形成可持续商业模式 — encourage open-source communities and enterprises to deepen open cooperation, form sustainable business models).
(b) OpenHarmony ecosystem devices exceed 1.35 billion units; HarmonyOS phones are the world’s third-largest mobile operating system; 3,200 ecosystem partners; 14,000+ code contributors; sector-branded OS derivatives (工鸿 Gong-Hong for manufacturing, 仪鸿 Yi-Hong for instrumentation) deployed at scale across automobiles, home appliances, metallurgy, petrochemicals, and other sectors. The “13.5亿台” (1.35 billion) figure is MIIT’s official count of devices running an OpenHarmony-derived OS, and the 世界第三大 (world’s third-largest) ranking is MIIT’s own framing, not an independent-analyst count.
(c) AI open-source cumulative downloads exceed 10 billion globally; the national AI open-source community (AtomGit-anchored, as documented in prior briefings) aggregates 11 million+ users and hosts 2 million+ projects.
From an institutional economics standpoint, the SCIO press-conference event matters for five reasons:
First, it documents the first SCIO-tier formalization of a three-pillar open-source industrial strategy. Prior MIIT open-source documentation (assembled in this cycle’s August 15–21 briefings on the OpenAtom partner-expansion layer, talent-certification layer, and community-formation layer) operated at the industry-sector-policy layer — foundation governance documents, certification frameworks, partner-structure announcements. This cycle’s SCIO press conference operates at the state-council-policy-discourse layer — the SCIO is the State Council’s own press-dissemination arm, and the “十五五” series is the formal Five-Year-Plan launch-sequencing channel. From an institutional economics standpoint, this layer-upgrade is a structural finding: MIIT’s open-source industrial strategy has been elevated from the industry-sector-policy layer to the state-council-policy-discourse layer, and the three-pillar vocabulary (强供给 / 促应用 / 育生态) becomes the formal lexical shell for the 15th Five-Year Plan’s open-source chapter.
Second, it documents the OpenHarmony “1.35 billion devices” figure as the MIIT-authorized institutional count of the OpenHarmony ecosystem. The 13.5亿台 figure is MIIT’s own count, not an independent-analyst estimate. From an institutional economics standpoint, the MIIT-authorized-count / open-ecosystem-size pairing is a structural finding: OpenHarmony’s ecosystem size is now an MIIT-authorized institutional metric, and the metric is being disseminated through the SCIO channel rather than through Huawei’s own marketing or OpenHarmony Community’s own reporting. This shifts the metric-authority locus from ecosystem-internal to state-council-external.
Third, it documents the sector-branded-OS-derivative (工鸿 / 仪鸿 / 电鸿 Dian-Hong for power-grid, 车鸿 Che-Hong for automotive) architecture as MIIT’s institutional vocabulary for OpenHarmony’s cross-sector deployment. The 工鸿 / 仪鸿 / 电鸿 / 车鸿 naming pattern — “industry-character + Hong” — is the same Chinese-prefix naming-politics instrument documented in prior briefings on the 2026 China Linux Kernel Developer Conference’s China-prefix naming. From an institutional economics standpoint, the sector-branded-derivative / naming-politics pairing is a structural finding: OpenHarmony’s cross-sector deployment is not a single-OS rollout but a multi-derivative sector-specific architecture, and each derivative is institutionally branded with a Chinese industry-character prefix.
Fourth, it documents the AtomGit-anchored national AI open-source community as the institutional anchor of China’s AI open-source downloads. The 10 billion cumulative downloads figure is MIIT’s own count, and the 11 million users / 2 million projects figure is MIIT’s own count of the national AI open-source community. From an institutional economics standpoint, the AtomGit-anchored-community / MIIT-authorized-count pairing is a structural finding: AtomGit (the Huawei-initiated Chinese GitHub alternative, documented in prior briefings as one of the four links in the Great-Divergence-2.0 open-source-infrastructure chain) is now institutionally positioned as the national AI open-source community anchor, and its user-project-download counts are MIIT-authorized institutional metrics.
Fifth, it creates an institutional bridge between the three-pillar industrial-strategy layer and the SCIO-tier policy-discourse layer. Prior MIIT open-source institutional-expansion documentation operated on the industry-sector-policy layer. This cycle’s SCIO press conference operates on the state-council-policy-discourse layer. From an institutional economics standpoint, this two-layer institutional-architecture is a structural finding: MIIT’s open-source program now has a documented two-layer institutional-architecture — industry-sector-policy layer + state-council-policy-discourse layer — rather than a single-layer industry-sector-policy architecture.
Sources:
央视网 CCTV News (2026-08-26) — 强供给 促应用 育生态 多维度发力乘势而上用好新一代信息技术 (Liu Yulin at SCIO press conference, republished on 开放原子) 政知见 / MIIT announcement (republished across 新浪财经, 搜狐, 微博) — 工信部：鸿蒙手机操作系统成为世界第三大手机操作系统，开源鸿蒙生态设备累计超13.5亿台 Sina News mirror — 工信部：鸿蒙手机操作系统成为世界第三大手机操作系统 Context: August 15–21 briefings — OpenAtom partner-expansion / talent-certification / community-formation layers 🏛️ 2026 OpenAtom Open-Source Ecosystem Conference (June 25–26, 2026) — 198 Donors / 600 Million Yuan Cumulative Funding / Mulan License-Family 6-Protocol Donation / Yi-Hong and M-Robots Community Launches — The OpenAtom Foundation’s Two-Year-Cycle Institutional Snapshot 2. 新华网 / Xinhua News (2026-06-25) and 科技日报 Science & Technology Daily (2026-06-26) coverage of the 2026 开放原子开源生态大会 (2026 OpenAtom Open-Source Ecosystem Conference), Beijing, June 25–26, 2026, theme “开源赋能产业，生态共筑未来” (Open Source Empowers Industry, Ecosystem Builds the Future).
The 2026 OpenAtom Open-Source Ecosystem Conference — the flagship annual event of the OpenAtom Foundation — convened on June 25–26, 2026, in Beijing. From an institutional economics standpoint, this cycle’s briefing documents five institutional announcements that together constitute the OpenAtom Foundation’s two-year-cycle institutional snapshot (the 2026 conference is the fourth edition since the foundation’s 2020 founding):
(a) Cumulative funding: 198 donors, over 600 million yuan cumulative fundraising since 2020. OpenAtom — the national-tier state-anchored open-source foundation, documented in prior briefings as the institutional anchor of China’s multi-foundation open-source architecture — reports 198 donating entities and over 600 million yuan cumulative fundraising since its 2020 founding. In 2026 to date: 9 new unrestricted donors joined, and 深开鸿 (ShenKaiHong / DeepKaiHong) and 拓维信息 (Talkweb Information) upgraded to platinum-tier donors — two companies that are themselves OpenHarmony ecosystem partners, making their platinum-tier upgrade a sector-reciprocal donor-ecosystem arrangement.
(b) Mulan license-family 6-protocol donation to the OpenAtom Foundation. The 2026 conference hosted the 木兰许可证族捐赠仪式 (Mulan License-Family Donation Ceremony), with six protocols covering distinct use-scenario categories. This is the first documented instance of a Chinese-characteristic open-source license family being formally donated to the OpenAtom Foundation, positioning OpenAtom as the institutional host of China’s bilingual-license governance architecture (as documented in Christopher K. Tong’s August 12 The Conversation article, which noted that MulanPSL 2.0 and the OpenAtom Model License 1.0 are both bilingual English-Chinese, with the Chinese version prevailing in cases of conflicting interpretation).
(c) 开放原子仪鸿开源社区 (OpenAtom Yi-Hong Instrumentation Open-Source Community) formally inaugurated. The Yi-Hong (仪鸿, “instrumentation + Hong”) community — the newest sector-branded derivative in OpenHarmony’s sector-branded-OS-derivative architecture (alongside Gong-Hong 工鸿 for manufacturing, Dian-Hong 电鸿 for power-grid, Che-Hong 车鸿 for automotive) — convened core members including 中国机械工业仪器仪表集团 (China Mechanical Industry Instrumentation Group), 中国华能 (China Huaneng), 中移物联网 (China Mobile IoT), and 拓维信息 (Talkweb) — spanning manufacturing, energy, IoT, and educational sectors.
(d) M-Robots (Robot Operating System) community formally launched; 龙蜥社区 (Anolis Linux Community) fully upgraded to an AI-native OS community; 龙架构社区 (LoongArch Community) and M-Robots launched to fill instruction-set and commercial-robotics open-source-ecosystem gaps.
(e) 源图 (YuanTu) — high-quality Skills dataset — released at the conference to address the domestic short-board in high-quality data supply for AI agents.
From an institutional economics standpoint, the 2026 OpenAtom conference matters for five reasons:
First, it documents the OpenAtom Foundation’s 198-donor / 600-million-yuan institutional-capital architecture as the two-year-cycle snapshot. From 2020 founding to mid-2026, OpenAtom has accumulated 198 donors and 600 million yuan — a six-year donor-capital trajectory that positions OpenAtom as China’s national-tier open-source foundation with a documented capital-inflow base. From an institutional economics standpoint, the donor-count / cumulative-funding pairing is a structural finding: OpenAtom’s institutional-capital architecture is now a documented metric, not a private-governance detail.
Second, it documents the Mulan license-family 6-protocol donation as the formal institutionalization of China’s bilingual-license governance architecture inside the OpenAtom Foundation. From an institutional economics standpoint, the Mulan-donation / OpenAtom-hosting pairing is a structural finding: the Mulan license family — the Chinese-characteristic open-source license family that Christopher Tong flagged as an element of China’s standards-setting project — is now institutionally hosted by the OpenAtom Foundation, not by the Mulan community itself. This advances the Mulan license family from the community-owned license to the foundation-hosted license, a governance-layer upgrade.
Third, it documents the Yi-Hong community launch as the newest sector-branded-OS-derivative in OpenHarmony’s sector-branded-derivative architecture. The Yi-Hong (instrumentation + Hong) community — covering manufacturing, energy, IoT, education — is the fourth documented sector-branded derivative in OpenHarmony’s architecture (Gong-Hong / Dian-Hong / Che-Hong / Yi-Hong). From an institutional economics standpoint, the Yi-Hong-launch / sector-branded-architecture pairing is a structural finding: OpenHarmony’s cross-sector deployment is now a documented four-derivative sector-specific architecture, each derivative branded with a Chinese industry-character prefix.
Fourth, it documents the M-Robots / LoongArch / Anolis-upgrade triple-announcement as OpenAtom’s frontier-technology expansion architecture. M-Robots addresses the commercial-robotics open-source-ecosystem gap, LoongArch addresses the domestic instruction-set open-source-ecosystem gap, and Anolis-upgrade addresses the AI-native-OS infrastructure gap. From an institutional economics standpoint, the triple-announcement / frontier-expansion pairing is a structural finding: OpenAtom’s 2026 frontier-expansion covers robotics, instruction-sets, and AI-native-OS infrastructure — three technology-frontier categories that were not covered in the foundation’s prior institutional-expansion documentation.
Fifth, it documents the YuanTu high-quality-Skills-dataset release as OpenAtom’s institutional entry into the AI-agent-data-supply layer. From an institutional economics standpoint, the YuanTu-release / data-supply-layer-entry pairing is a structural finding: the OpenAtom Foundation has now entered the AI-agent-data-supply layer as an institutional actor, alongside its prior institutional presence in the AI-model-release layer (via AtomGit-hosted models) and the AI-governance layer (via CAICT-adjacent standards bodies).

From an institutional economics standpoint, this cross-surface republishing is a structural finding: Tong’s standards-setting framing of Chinese open-source policy — which argues that “the countries that lead the technical and legal standards governing open-source technology will gain a competitive edge for decades to come” — now has a documented two-surface institutional-reception architecture (The Conversation syndicated-academic surface + Asia Times international-asia-affairs surface). Sources:
Asia Times (Christopher Tong, 2026-08-17) — China’s shaping the future of open-source technology including AI The Conversation (Christopher Tong, 2026-08-12) — China is shaping the future of open-source technology — including AI Context: August 16 briefing — Tong’s article as the first academic framing of Chinese open-source policy as standards-setting 🏛️ Commentary — Three-Pillar Strategy / Sector-Braned Architecture / Standards-Framing Reception: A Three-Layer Institutional Architecture Has Now Been Documented for China’s Open-Source Program This cycle’s briefing documents three simultaneous institutional moves that together reveal a three-layer institutional architecture of China’s open-source program that prior briefings did not document:
MIIT Liu Yulin three-pillar industrial strategy / SCIO-tier policy-discourse formalization / OpenHarmony 1.35-billion-devices institutional count (item 1) — the first SCIO-tier formalization of MIIT’s open-source industrial strategy under the three-pillar vocabulary (强供给 / 促应用 / 育生态), and the first MIIT-authorized institutional count of the OpenHarmony ecosystem at 1.35 billion devices, advanced through the SCIO channel.
2026 OpenAtom conference 198-donor / 600-million-yuan / Mulan-donation / Yi-Hong-launch / YuanTu-dataset (item 2) — the OpenAtom Foundation’s two-year-cycle institutional snapshot, documenting its 198-donor / 600-million-yuan capital architecture, the Mulan license-family 6-protocol donation (governance-layer upgrade for Chinese-characteristic bilingual licenses), the Yi-Hong community launch (fourth sector-branded-OS-derivative in OpenHarmony’s architecture), and the YuanTu dataset release (OpenAtom’s institutional entry into the AI-agent-data-supply layer).
Tong’s August 12 academic article reaching Asia Times on August 17 (item 3) — the cross-surface extension of Tong’s standards-setting framing of Chinese open-source policy from The Conversation’s syndicated-academic surface to Asia Times’ international-asia-affairs surface, creating a documented two-surface institutional-reception architecture for the standards-setting framing.
The institutional reading: these three moves do not cancel each other out. They operate on three distinct institutional layers — state-council-policy-discourse (item 1), national-foundation-institutional-capital (item 2), and international-academic-reception (item 3) — and together they form a three-layer institutional architecture of China’s open-source program that prior briefings did not document.
The MIIT / SCIO / OpenAtom layer-pairing (items 1 and 2) is a state-policy / national-foundation layer-pairing: the SCIO press conference formalizes the three-pillar industrial strategy and MIIT-authorized metrics; the OpenAtom conference formalizes the foundation’s capital architecture, license-hosting role, and frontier-expansion coverage. They operate on two distinct but mutually-reinforcing institutional layers — state-policy + national-foundation. The Tong / Asia Times layer (item 3) is an international-academic-reception layer, and its cross-surface extension (The Conversation + Asia Times) is a framing-reception event rather than a policy-formalization event.
The September 30, 2026 Black Duck deadline (documented August 24, three weeks away) remains the nearest institutional milestone. This cycle’s three-layer institutional architecture — state-policy / national-foundation / international-academic-reception — is now the operating architecture of China’s open-source institutional ecosystem through at least Q4 2026. The Black Duck compliance-vacuum and the MIIT three-pillar / OpenAtom capital / Tong standards-setting moves form a layered institutional-complex: Black Duck’s exit creates a compliance-vacuum; MIIT’s three-pillar strategy formalizes the open-source industrial policy; OpenAtom’s capital architecture formalizes the foundation-governance layer; Tong’s standards-setting framing formalizes the international-academic-reception layer. Whether the four layers converge into a documented institutional-replacement architecture or diverge into a documented institutional gap is the defining institutional question for Q4 2026.

SCIO press conference follow-up: sector-level 15th Five-Year-Plan open-source policy documents OpenHarmony 1.35-billion-devices figure: independent-analyst verification attempts OpenAtom Foundation: September donor-aggregation signals Black Duck September 30 closure: enterprise-customer migration signals Tong’s article: further cross-surface republishing (international-policy outlets)

China Open Source Daily — 2026-08-27 🏛️ CAICT’s ATH Protocol Crosses into 《中国改革》(China Reform) — A First-Documented Institutional-Legitimacy Threshold for China’s Agent-Governance Technical Standard 1. OSCAR可信开源 (OSCAR Trustworthy Open Source, WeChat) — “ATH开源协议相关内容被《中国改革》杂志智能体治理专题文章借鉴论述” (Content relating to the ATH open-source protocol has been cited in 《中国改革》’s special-section article on intelligent-agent governance), republished 2026-08-25, citing 《中国改革》 Issue 448 dated 2026-07-01
The OSCAR可信开源 (OSCAR Trustworthy Open Source) WeChat official account (mp.weixin.qq.com/s/C2dgjB09WH5cgsvH4ADnhA) has disclosed, on 2026-08-25, that CAICT’s ATH (Agent Trusted Handshake) protocol — the agent-governance technical standard launched by 中国信通院 (CAICT) on May 7, 2026, jointly with Tencent, Huawei, China Unicom, China Mobile Jiutian, CUHK-Shenzhen, and ZTE, and released open-source on both AtomGit and GitHub — has been formally cited by 《中国改革》 (China Reform) in its July 2026 cover-feature special section on intelligent-agent governance (Issue 448, Issue 4 of 2026, dated 2026-07-01).
Context on the citing vehicle — 《中国改革》 (China Reform): 《中国改革》is Caixin Media’s governance-policy flagship journal, published by the same editorial organization as 财新 (Caixin Weekly). Its Issue 448’s cover feature (“对外投资新规面面观” — new regulations on outbound investment from all angles) is a policy-and-institutional governance publication, not a technology-journal publication. Its “Governance / 治理” section, in which ATH is cited, is the publication’s senior-academic policy-discourse surface.
Context on the senior-academic co-anchor — 季卫东 (Ji Weidong): In the same Issue 448 “Governance / 治理” section, 季卫东 (Ji Weidong) — SJTU senior academic professor, director of the SJTU China-Institute-of-Law-and-Society, and director of the AI-Governance-and-Law Research Center — authored the section’s lead institutional-economics article: “智能体治理的复杂性与法律驾驭” (The Complexity of Intelligent-Agent Governance and Legal Mastery), arguing that “how to effectively prevent social risks amid rapid technology iteration requires institutional innovation through specialized legislation targeting intelligent agents.” In the same Issue, 傅蔚冈 (Fu Weigang) authored a companion piece, “智能体时代的信任” (Trust in the Age of Intelligent Agents) — establishing Issue 448 as a full-section institutional-economics treatment of agent governance, not a technology-news column.
Institutional significance: This is the first documented institutional-legitimacy event that carries CAICT’s ATH agent-governance protocol from the industry-standards layer into the national policy-discourse layer — a structurally new cross-layer legitimacy-crossing that prior briefings did not document.
From an institutional economics perspective, the ATH / 《中国改革》 event matters for four reasons:
First, it documents a layer-crossing move in CAICT’s agent-governance institutional-expansion. Prior CAICT agent-governance documentation (documented in this cycle’s August 25–26 briefings on the Token-Factory compute-standards apparatus and the GOAI movement-anchor appointment) operated on the industry-standards layer — certification frameworks, grading systems, competition-venue appointments. ATH, launched May 2026, was a technical-standard-object released on AtomGit+GitHub. This cycle’s 《中国改革》 citation is the first documented instance in which a CAICT agent-governance technical-standard-object has been cited inside a national-policy-discourse publication’s institutional-economics special section — a layer-crossing event that moves CAICT’s agent-governance institutional-expansion from the industry-standards layer to the national-policy-discourse layer.
Second, it documents OSCAR (Open-Source Community and AI Resource) Trustworthy Open Source as the legitimacy-broker for the ATH / 《中国改革》 crossing. The disclosure source is OSCAR可信开源 (OSCAR Trustworthy Open Source) itself — OSCAR, not CAICT directly, is the entity publishing the disclosure that 《中国改革》 has cited ATH. From an institutional economics standpoint, this disclosure-source pattern is a structural finding: OSCAR functions as the public-relations / legitimacy-broker node for the ATH standard’s journey into national-policy-discourse, mediating between CAICT’s technical-standard production and 《中国改革》’s institutional-economics reception.
Third, it creates an institutional bridge between the agent-governance technical-standard object and a senior-academic institutional-economics treatment co-located in the same publication. ATH is cited inside Issue 448, which in the same “Governance / 治理” section also carries Ji Weidong’s “智能体治理的复杂性与法律驾驭” — Ji Weidong is one of China’s senior institutional-economics legal scholars (SJTU senior professor, China-Institute-of-Law-and-Society director, AI-Governance-and-Law Research Center director), whose prior institutional-economics work on AI governance is documented in the August 2019 SJTU AI-rule-of-law forum coverage. From an institutional economics standpoint, the ATH-technical-standard / Ji-Weidong-institutional-economics co-location inside the same 《中国改革》special section is a structural finding: CAICT’s agent-governance technical standard is now institutionally co-located with senior-academic institutional-economics treatment in the same national-policy-discourse surface — a dual-anchor legitimacy structure that prior briefings did not observe.
Fourth, it advances the ATH protocol’s institutional-architecture from the open-source-release object to the policy-cited object. ATH was released open-source on May 7, 2026, on AtomGit+GitHub (both platforms — a “dual-release” pattern consistent with CAICT’s prior AtomGit-first / GitHub-second release architecture documented in August 2026 briefings). This cycle’s 《中国改革》 citation is the first documented instance of ATH being cited by a national-policy-discourse publication — advancing ATH’s institutional-architecture from the open-source-release object to the policy-cited object, a structurally new institutional-stage that prior briefings did not document.

From an institutional economics standpoint, this rhetorical-structure / gross-margin-empirical pairing is a structural finding with implications for how the “going-global as institutional rhetoric” thesis will be tested and refined in coming briefings.

⚠️ Editorial note: The open source ecosystem in China operates under a distinct institutional framework — characterized by state-led initiatives, intranet-like boundaries, and top-down governance. Readers should be aware that this context differs from the community-driven open source model common in other regions. The term “open source” as used in Chinese media may refer to practices that diverge from the conventional definition.
China Open Source Daily — 2026-08-26 🏛️ CAICT + COPU Release the “Token Factory · Intelligence-Computing Capability Grading Evaluation System” — A State-Anchored, Five-Tier Administrative-Grading Apparatus for China’s Proliferating AI Compute-Facility Market 1. COPU / 云计算开源产业联盟 (Cloud Computing Open Source Industry Alliance, WeChat) — “重磅发布！中国信通院正式发布’Token工厂·智算能力分级评价体系’” (Major release! CAICT formally releases the “Token Factory · Intelligence-Computing Capability Grading Evaluation System”)
The COPU (Cloud Computing Open Source Industry Alliance) WeChat official account (mp.weixin.qq.com/s/dye8oZSoeQpaWY8OQ542ew) published on 2026-08-25 the formal announcement that the CAICT Cloud Computing and Digitalization Research Institute (中国信通院云计算与数字化研究所) has released the first “Token Factory · Intelligence-Computing Capability Grading Evaluation System” (Token工厂·智算能力分级评价体系) — an authoritative certification apparatus positioning CAICT as the standard-setter for China’s proliferating Token-Factory compute-facility market.
What the system does, per the WeChat announcement: the evaluation system constructs a five-dimension capability framework (Token-production-capacity energy-efficiency / 交付服务 delivery-service / 智能运营 intelligent-operations / 安全合规 security-compliance / and one further dimension documented as macro-operations coverage) and a five-tier grading scale T1–T5 (T1 起步级 startup / T2 标准级 standard / T3 先进级 advanced / T4 领先级 leading / T5 标杆级 benchmark). The evaluation method is a tripartite architecture: document review + on-site performance testing in the Token Factory’s real production environment + expert-panel review. The system operates on a dual-track mode — operational-class (运行类) for already-operating Token Factories, and design-class (设计类) for facilities under construction — enabling even pre-launch facilities to obtain a certified tier for marketing and policy-alignment purposes.
Institutional significance: This is the first documented move by CAICT that converts China’s Token-Factory compute-facility market from an unregulated “price-per-token” competition surface into a state-anchored, certificate-based governance surface — a structurally new administrative-standards apparatus that prior cycles did not document.
From an institutional economics perspective, the Token-Factory grading system matters for four reasons:
First, it creates the first documented administrative-standards object for China’s Token-Factory market. Prior to this cycle’s announcement, the Chinese Token-Factory market — populated by the three state-owned telcos, the leading commercial cloud providers, and local state-asset-platform facilities — operated without a unified capability standard. Per the WeChat announcement: “当前Token工厂产业仍处于发展初期，行业内尚未形成统一的能力评价标准” (the Token-Factory industry is still in its early stage; no unified capability-evaluation standard has been formed). CAICT’s system fills this standards gap by providing a state-anchored, five-tier, five-dimension grading apparatus — a structurally new administrative-standards object that converts the Token-Factory market from an informal price-competition surface into a formally graded certification surface.
Second, it converts the dominant market-comparison metric from price-per-token to capability-tier. Per the WeChat announcement, the system is designed to redirect industry competition from “比单价” (compare per-unit token price) toward “比产能、比质量、比能效、比服务” (compare capacity / quality / energy-efficiency / service). From an institutional economics standpoint, this metric-substitution move — replacing price with state-certified capability-tier as the dominant comparison axis — is a structural finding: CAICT is not just rating Token Factories; it is redefining how Token-Factory quality is institutionally recognized. This is the same pattern as CAICT’s prior administrative-standards work on open-source-compliance evaluation (documented in the August 24 briefing’s Black Duck exit commentary) and COPU’s enterprise open-source maturity assessments — state authority substitutes for market price as the primary signaling instrument.
Third, it creates an institutional bridge to the Black Duck exit (August 24 briefing, compliance-vacuum narrative). Black Duck’s exit removed the only Western-sourced, enterprise-grade open-source compliance-governance vendor inside China. CAICT’s Token-Factory grading apparatus is on a different institutional layer (compute-facility capability rather than open-source-license compliance) but operates through the same administrative-standards mechanism — state certification as the primary recognition instrument. From an institutional economics standpoint, this compliance-vacuum / compute-grading pairing reveals that China’s open-source institutional ecosystem is experiencing two simultaneous standards moves on two different layers — compliance-standards withdrawal (item 1, August 24) and compute-standards addition (item 1, this cycle) — that co-exist as a dual-layer standards trajectory.
Fourth, it advances CAICT’s institutional-expansion from the open-source-compliance layer to the compute-facility layer. Prior CAICT institutional-expansion documentation operated at the open-source-compliance and open-source-ecosystem-assessment layers (documented in the August 16–24 briefings’ institutional-architecture baselines). This cycle’s Token-Factory grading move operates at the compute-facility layer — the Token-Factory grading apparatus is a layer-ascent move that extends CAICT’s institutional-expansion from open-source-compliance to compute-facility-grading. From an institutional economics standpoint, this is a layer-ascent move: CAICT’s institutional-expansion has extended from the open-source-compliance layer to the compute-facility layer — a two-layer institutional-architecture that prior cycles did not document.
Sources:
COPU / 云计算开源产业联盟 (WeChat) — 重磅发布！中国信通院正式发布"Token工厂·智算能力分级评价体系" AIHUB (aisperf.caict.ac.cn) — AISHPERF基准：2026年第一批"可信智算-高效能Token服务能力"新一轮评估正式启动 (parallel CAICT Token-service-capability evaluation initiative) Context: August 24 briefing — Black Duck exit (compliance-vacuum / compute-grading pairing) 🏛️ COPU Honorary Chairman Lu Shouqun Invited to Serve on GOAI World AI Open-Source Competition Chairmanship Group — A Structurally New Institutional-Bridge Appointment 2. COPU / 云计算开源产业联盟 (WeChat) — “陆首群应邀出任GOAI世界人工智能开源大赛主席团成员” (Lu Shouqun invited to serve on GOAI World AI Open-Source Competition chairmanship group)
The COPU (Cloud Computing Open Source Industry Alliance) WeChat official account (mp.weixin.qq.com/s/jV3S-XL3ycWG3up9_EaISg) announced on 2026-08-25 that Lu Shouqun (陆首群) — COPU’s honorary chairman (名誉主席) and one of the important promoters of the Chinese and global open-source movements — has been invited to serve as a core member of the GOAI (World Artificial Intelligence Open-Source Competition) chairmanship group, providing guidance on the competition’s strategic direction and ecosystem construction.
What GOAI is, per the WeChat announcement: the GOAI World AI Open-Source Competition (世界人工智能开源大赛) was formally launched at the 杭州云谷中心 (Hangzhou Cloud Valley Center); hosted by the 杭州开源人工智能基金会 (Hangzhou Open-Source AI Foundation); with a 5,000,000 RMB (5-million-RMB) cash prize pool; four competition tracks (新智基座 / New Intelligence Foundation / 无界应用 / Boundless Application / 前沿探索 / Frontier Exploration / 具身未来 / Embodied Future); open to global developer registration.
Institutional significance: This is the first documented institutional-bridge appointment that converts Lu Shouqun from the COPU-internal governance axis to a GOAI-foundation external-anchor axis — a structurally new role-expansion event that validates the “COPU-chairman-as-ecosystem-bridge” hypothesis with a concrete appointment.
From an institutional economics perspective, Lu Shouqun’s GOAI appointment matters for four reasons:
First, it documents Lu Shouqun’s institutional-expansion beyond the COPU venue. Prior Lu Shouqun institutional documentation operated exclusively at the COPU-internal axis — COPU meetings, COPU governance structure, COPU open-source-maturity assessments (documented throughout the August 2026 briefings’ institutional-architecture baselines, and as the core institutional specimen of the 《开源之史》 / “The History of Open Source” research program). This cycle’s GOAI appointment documents Lu Shouqun as a cross-institutional actor — simultaneously COPU honorary chairman and GOAI chairmanship-group core member. From an institutional economics standpoint, this cross-institutional role-expansion is a layer-addition event that expands Lu Shouqun’s institutional-architecture from a COPU-internal object to a COPU-plus-GOAI dual-axis object.
Second, it validates the “COPU-chairman-as-ecosystem-bridge” hypothesis with a concrete appointment. Prior institutional-analysis cycles hypothesized that COPU’s chairmanship and honorary-chairmanship roles functioned as ecosystem-bridge nodes connecting the COPU governance axis to adjacent open-source institutional objects (BAAI, CAICT, CCF, etc.). Lu Shouqun’s GOAI appointment provides the first concrete empirical observation of this bridging role operating in a competition-venue context rather than a governance-venue context. From an institutional economics standpoint, this COPU-chairman-as-GOAI-anchor observation is a structural finding with implications for how COPU’s chairmanship-ecosystem-bridge hypothesis will be narrated in coming cycles.
Third, it creates an institutional bridge between the COPU governance axis and the Hangzhou municipal open-source-AI axis. The GOAI World AI Open-Source Competition is hosted by the Hangzhou Open-Source AI Foundation — a municipal-foundation institutional object (Hangzhou-specific, not national). Lu Shouqun’s appointment to the GOAI chairmanship group creates the first documented institutional bridge between the COPU national-governance axis and the Hangzhou municipal-open-source-AI axis. From an institutional economics standpoint, this national-governance / municipal-foundation bridge is a structural finding: COPU’s institutional-expansion is not just horizontal (peer-to-peer foundation connections) but vertical (national-to-municipal governance-axis bridging).
Fourth, it advances the “open-source-movement-promoter-as-institutional-anchor” role-assertion pattern with a competition-venue manifestation. Prior role-assertion documentation positioned Lu Shouqun as an open-source-movement-promoter on COPU governance-venue stages. This cycle’s GOAI appointment positions Lu Shouqun as the same institutional role on a competition-venue stage — a structurally distinct venue type (competitive rather than governance). From an institutional economics standpoint, this governance-venue / competition-venue pairing is a structural finding with implications for how COPU’s movement-promoter role-assertion will be narrated in coming cycles.
Sources:
COPU / 云计算开源产业联盟 (WeChat) — 陆首群应邀出任GOAI世界人工智能开源大赛主席团成员 Context: Prior August 2026 briefings — Lu Shouqun as COPU institutional specimen 🔍 Huawei — Ascend CANN HCCL Communication-Library Innovation Contest Opens Northeast-Region Registration at Harbin Institute of Technology — An Empirical Observation of Huawei’s Talent-Pipeline Institution 3. 黄大年茶思屋 (Huang Danian Chaisi Wu / Huang Danian Tea-Thought House, Huawei-strategy-unit-affiliated WeChat) — “昇腾 CANN HCCL通信库创新大赛东北赛区报名开启” (Ascend CANN HCCL Communication-Library Innovation Contest — Northeast region registration now open)
The 黄大年茶思屋 (Huang Danian Tea-Thought House) WeChat official account (mp.weixin.qq.com/s/BHjyFEg_JtuiyP72TiLWkQ, published 2026-08-20) documents that the Ascend CANN HCCL Communication-Library Innovation Contest — Northeast-region round has opened registration, hosted by 哈尔滨工业大学 (Harbin Institute of Technology / HIT), open to science-and-engineering students at Northeast-region universities across communications, computer-science, electronic-information, and mathematics majors; registration runs August 17 – September 6, 2026.
Prize and incentive structure, per the WeChat announcement: first prize × 2 teams: 20,000 RMB + certificate; second prize × 5 teams: 10,000 RMB + certificate; third prize × 10 teams: 5,000 RMB + certificate; HCCL Community Special Contribution Award × 10 teams: 1,000 RMB (awarded based on issue and PR quality and quantity on gitcode.com/cann/hccl and gitcode.com/cann/hcomm). Beyond cash and certificates, winning teams receive Huawei fast-track hiring (华为专场优招), top-talent-summit invitations, Huawei-base deep-tour access, Ascend latest-product experience, and one-on-one mentorship from senior engineers.
Institutional significance: This is the first documented regional-round registration opening of the Ascend CANN HCCL Innovation Contest — a concrete empirical observation of Huawei’s talent-pipeline institution routing university developers into the Ascend + CANN + GitCode ecosystem through certificates + prizes + fast-track-hiring incentive stacking.
From an institutional economics perspective, the HCCL Contest Northeast-region round matters for four reasons:
First, it documents Huawei’s talent-pipeline institution operating at the regional-university level. Prior Huawei institutional-expansion documentation operated at the national-forum level (CCF China Open Source Conference — August 25 briefing; AtomGit / 仓颉 platform launches; MindSpore framework governance). This cycle’s HCCL Contest Northeast-region round operates at the regional-university level — a Harbin Institute of Technology-hosted, Northeast-region-universities-targeted registration round. From an institutional economics standpoint, this national-forum / regional-university pairing is a layer-descent move that documents Huawei’s talent-pipeline institution operating at a granular, geographically-targeted layer prior cycles did not observe.
Second, it documents Huawei’s “community-contribution-as-recruitment-funnel-input” incentive design in concrete form. The contest’s HCCL Community Special Contribution Award (特别贡献奖) explicitly rewards issue and PR quality and quantity on Huawei’s own GitCode repositories — gitcode.com/cann/hccl and gitcode.com/cann/hcomm. From an institutional economics standpoint, this contribution-reward-to-Huawei-owned-platform design is a structural finding: the “open-source contribution” that the contest incentivizes is contribution to Huawei’s own code-hosting platform (GitCode) and Huawei’s own compiler stack (HCCL/CANN), not contribution to a global open-source community. This is the same institutional pattern documented in prior cycles’ discussion of Huawei’s “开源” (open-source) as opening Huawei’s own system rather than opening to the global community — but now observed at a concrete regional-university contest instance rather than at an abstract platform level.
Third, it creates an institutional bridge to Huawei’s CANN open-source move (August 25 briefing, institutional-architecture baseline). The CANN open-source move at the 2026 CCF China Open Source Conference (August 25 briefing) formally converted Huawei’s CANN compiler stack from a proprietary-vendor-stack object to an open-source object. The HCCL Contest Northeast-region round operationalizes that open-source object into a university-talent acquisition surface — students compete on open-sourced CANN-HCCL code, contribute to GitCode-hosted HCCL repositories, and are funneled into Huawei fast-track hiring. From an institutional economics standpoint, this compiler-open-source / contest-talent-pipeline pairing is a structural finding: Huawei’s CANN open-source move is not just a compiler-institution object but a talent-acquisition object — the open-source compiler stack becomes a recruitment-funnel input surface.
Fourth, it advances Huawei’s institutional-expansion from the software-institution layer to the talent-pipeline layer. Prior Huawei institutional-expansion documentation (documented in the August 25 briefing’s CANN commentary) operated at the hardware layer (Ascend silicon), the software-vendor layer (MindSpore, MindFormers), and the software-institution layer (CANN open-source). This cycle’s HCCL Contest Northeast-region round operates at the talent-pipeline layer — a structurally new layer that converts university developers into the Ascend+CANN+GitCode ecosystem through certificates + prizes + fast-track-hiring. From an institutional economics standpoint, this is a layer-ascent move: Huawei’s institutional-expansion has extended from the hardware / software-vendor / software-institution layers to the talent-pipeline layer — a four-layer institutional-architecture that prior cycles did not document.

⚠️ Editorial note: The open source ecosystem in China operates under a distinct institutional framework — characterized by state-led initiatives, intranet-like boundaries, and top-down governance. Readers should be aware that this context differs from the community-driven open source model common in other regions. The term “open source” as used in Chinese media may refer to practices that diverge from the conventional definition.
China Open Source Daily — 2026-08-25 🏛️ Huawei CANN Compiler Stack Formally Open-Source at 2026 CCF China Open Source Conference — Completes a Two-Source Confirmation of the Domestic AI-Chip-Compiler Open-Source Institutional Claim 1. CCF开源发展技术委员会 (CCF Open Source Development Technology Committee) — 2026 CCF China Open Source Conference, CANN Forum (“CANN全面开源开放，共赢AI技术生态” 分论坛 / “CANN Fully Open Source, Shared AI Technology Ecosystem” Forum)
The CCF Open Source Development Technology Committee hosted a “CANN Fully Open Source, Shared AI Technology Ecosystem” sub-forum at the 2026 CCF China Open Source Conference, as documented through the WeChat article mp.weixin.qq.com/s/fvB1fR1i-LuMPBPrbjmsFQ (title extracted via the WeChat article extractor, sourced through the China Daily English Input repository, 2026-08-24), and corroborated through SearXNG indexing (163.com reprint 163.com/news/article/L4K3P4N600019UD6.html and 36kr newsflash 36kr.com/newsflashes/3409838718127746, title: “华为宣布CANN全面开源开放，共建昇腾生态” / “Huawei announces CANN fully open-sourced, co-building Ascend ecosystem”). Per the WeChat digest: “本次分论坛围绕 CANN 异构计算架构的开源开放与生态建设展开，来自华为、南京大学、魔芯科技等产业界与高校的专家齐聚现场” (This sub-forum covered the open-source release and ecosystem construction of Huawei’s CANN heterogeneous-compute architecture; experts from Huawei, Nanjing University, Magic-Core (魔芯科技), and other industry and academic institutions gathered on site).
CANN — Compute Architecture for Neural Networks — is Huawei’s proprietary heterogeneous-compute compiler and runtime stack for its Ascend AI-chip series. It occupies the same institutional position relative to Ascend silicon as NVIDIA’s CUDA occupies relative to NVIDIA GPU silicon: it is the compiler-and-runtime layer that converts hardware capacity into developer-accessible capability. Per SearXNG-indexed ifeng.com tech coverage (“华为甘斌：开源开放，共赢Agentic时代” / “Huawei Gan Bin: Open Source and Openness, Win the Agentic Era Together”), Gan Bin (甘斌) — Huawei’s senior executive overseeing the Ascend stack — publicly framed the open-source move as the institutional precondition for entering the “Agentic Era.”
Institutional significance: This is the first documented institutional move that shifts Huawei’s Ascend AI-chip ecosystem from a proprietary-vendor-stack architecture (single-vendor-compiler, single-vendor-runtime, single-vendor-model-library) to an open-compiler-institution architecture — completing, within a 5-day window, a two-source cross-institutional confirmation of the “domestic AI-chip compiler open-source” institutional claim alongside BAAI’s FlagOS/FlagTree CUDA-Tile-IR integration (documented August 20 briefing).
From an institutional economics perspective, Huawei’s CANN open-source move matters for four reasons:
First, it creates the first documented open-compiler-institution object in China’s domestic AI-chip-compiler ecosystem. Prior Huawei CANN documentation positioned the stack as an internal-vendor property — Huawei controls the compiler, the runtime, the model library, and the developer tooling; external developers access Ascend silicon through Huawei’s proprietary stack, which is institutionally equivalent to a vendor-locked architecture (the same structure as NVIDIA’s CUDA lock-in, but on the domestic side). This cycle’s CCF-Conference documentation introduces CANN as an open-source object — the compiler stack is now a public institutional object, not a vendor-property object. From an institutional economics standpoint, this is a layer-shift move: the institutional-architecture object of Huawei’s Ascend ecosystem has shifted from “proprietary compiler stack” to “open compiler institution.”
Second, it completes a two-source cross-institutional confirmation of the “domestic AI-chip compiler open-source” institutional claim. Within 5 days of this cycle’s documentation, BAAI’s Zhongzhi team integrated CUDA Tile IR into FlagOS’s multi-chip unified compiler FlagTree (August 20 briefing, institutional-architecture baseline: FlagOS as BAAI’s open-computing platform). Huawei’s CANN open-source move at the CCF Conference (this cycle) is the second-source confirmation of the same institutional claim — from a different actor (Huawei, commercial-enterprise) operating in parallel with BAAI (state-anchored research institution). From an institutional economics standpoint, this two-source parallel-actor confirmation is a structural finding: the “domestic AI-chip compiler open-source” institutional claim is now not a single-actor claim (BAAI only) but a two-actor parallel claim (BAAI + Huawei) — a structurally stronger institutional claim.
Third, it moves Huawei’s institutional-expansion from the hardware layer to the software-institution layer. Prior Huawei institutional-expansion documentation operated at the hardware layer (Ascend silicon, GPU-class chips, domestic-compute infrastructure) and the software-vendor layer (MindSpore framework, MindFormers models — August 16–24 briefings’ institutional-architecture baselines). This cycle’s CANN open-source move operates at the software-institution layer — the compiler stack becomes an open institution, not a proprietary tool. From an institutional economics standpoint, this is a layer-ascent move: Huawei’s institutional-expansion has extended from the hardware layer and the software-vendor layer to the software-institution layer — a three-layer institutional-architecture that prior cycles did not document.
Fourth, it institutionalizes Huawei’s role as a compiler-stack governance actor in the domestic AI-chip ecosystem. By formally open-sourcing CANN at a CCF-conference forum — a national open-source institutional venue — Huawei positions itself not just as an Ascend-silicon vendor but as a compiler-stack governance actor. From an institutional economics standpoint, this is a role-assertion move with implications for how the domestic AI-chip-compiler ecosystem will be governed in coming cycles: Huawei is now not just a silicon provider but a compiler-institution participant, alongside BAAI.

CCF开源发展技术委员会 (WeChat) — 【2026 CCF中国开源大会】CANN全面开源开放，共赢AI技术生态分论坛成功举办 163.com (reprint) — CANN全面开源开放，共赢AI技术生态 36kr (newsflash) — 华为宣布CANN全面开源开放，共建昇腾生态 ifeng.com (tech) — 华为甘斌：开源开放，共赢Agentic时代 Context: August 20 briefing — BAAI FlagOS/FlagTree CUDA-Tile-IR integration (two-source parallel-actor confirmation) 🏛️ Tiangong Kaiwu Foundation × MoLe (Modelers) Community Strategic Partnership — First Institutional Bridge Between a State-Anchored “Chinese-Characteristic” Open-Source Foundation and a CSDN-Anchored Developer-Platform Community 2. 天工开物开源基金会 (Tiangong Kaiwu Open Source Foundation) + 魔乐社区 (MoLe / Modelers Community) — “构建中国特色AI开源协作新范式｜天工开物携手魔乐社区共建开源产业生态” (Constructing a Chinese-Characteristic AI Open-Source Collaboration Paradigm: Tiangong Kaiwu Joins MoLe Community to Co-build Open-Source Industrial Ecosystem)
The Tiangong Kaiwu Open Source Foundation and the MoLe (Modelers) Community have announced a formal strategic partnership, as documented through the WeChat article mp.weixin.qq.com/s/vfWzdy9ywhMTs1pn5aT5OQ (title extracted via the WeChat article extractor, sourced through the China Daily English Input repository, 2026-08-24). Per the WeChat digest: “天工开物开源基金会与魔乐社区正式达成战略合作，携手共建AI开源生态” (Tiangong Kaiwu Open Source Foundation and MoLe Community formally reached a strategic partnership, jointly constructing the AI open-source ecosystem).
Institutional identities of the two partners:
Tiangong Kaiwu Open Source Foundation (天工开物开源基金会) — a state-anchored open-source foundation named after Song Yingxing’s 1637 encyclopedic work “Tiangong Kaiwu” (天工开物, “The Exploitation of the Works of Nature”); operates in the same institutional family as the OpenAtom Foundation, CCF Open Source Committee, and BAAI FlagOpen — but with a distinct identity anchored in the “Chinese-characteristic” (中国特色) framing. Per SearXNG indexing and the official tiangong.earth portal: Tiangong Kaiwu publishes open-source projects in sustainable-development AI (Kaiwu AI, LLM tools, RAG frameworks) staffed by Tsinghua University developers.
MoLe Community (魔乐社区 / Modelers) — per its official portal (modelers.csdn.net), MoLe describes itself as “一个中立、公益的人工智能社区” (a neutral, public-welfare AI community) providing model hosting, exhibition, and application-synergy services for AI developers and enthusiasts; governed through a council structure (理事会方式运作) by the full industry chain “commonly built, commonly operated, commonly enjoyed” (共同建设、共同运营、共同享有). Per SearXNG indexing, MoLe operates under the CSDN (China Software Developer Network) organizational umbrella and hosts an active model-hosting platform (Qwen, GLM, MiniMax, Intern-S2, and other open-weight models). It also operates a series of developer-acquisition contests: the “魔乐AI乐构计划” (model-quantization challenge), “国产算力应用创新大赛” (200,000 RMB prize pool, domestic-compute-application innovation contest), and “AI赋能·智汇高校实训营” (AI-for-X university training camp with Huawei Ascend technical support).
Institutional significance: This is the first documented institutional bridge between a state-anchored “Chinese-characteristic” open-source foundation (Tiangong Kaiwu) and a CSDN-anchored developer-platform community (MoLe) — converting the Tiangong Kaiwu Foundation’s institutional-expansion mechanism from a project-publication object (prior documentation) into a community-partnership object, with the explicit framing “构建中国特色AI开源协作新范式” (constructing a Chinese-characteristic AI open-source collaboration paradigm).
From an institutional economics perspective, the Tiangong Kaiwu × MoLe partnership matters for four reasons:
First, it adds a third institutional-expansion layer to Tiangong Kaiwu’s institutional-architecture. Prior Tiangong Kaiwu documentation positioned the foundation’s institutional-expansion at (a) the project-publication layer (Tiangong AI open-source projects — Kaiwu AI, LLM tools, RAG frameworks); (b) the open-weight-model-hosting layer (models hosted on AtomGit, MoLe, and ModelScope — August 23–24 briefings’ institutional-architecture baselines). This cycle’s MoLe partnership introduces a third institutional-expansion layer — the community-partnership layer — in which Tiangong Kaiwu does not just publish projects or host models but strategically partners with a developer-platform community (MoLe) to co-construct the “AI open-source industrial ecosystem.” From an institutional economics standpoint, this is a three-layer institutional-architecture — a structurally new form that prior cycles did not surface.
Second, it operationalizes the “中国特色” (Chinese-characteristic) framing as a concrete institutional instrument. The partnership’s explicit title — “构建中国特色AI开源协作新范式” — is the first documented usage of the “中国特色” framing as a partnership-title framing (as opposed to a project-description framing or a policy-document framing). From an institutional economics standpoint, this is a framing-instrumentalization move: the “Chinese-characteristic” framing is being converted from an abstract discourse object (previously documented in policy texts and project descriptions) into a concrete partnership-title instrument — a structurally new institutional usage with implications for how other “Chinese-characteristic” open-source partnerships might be framed in coming cycles.
Third, it creates an institutional bridge to the OpenAtom Foundation’s institutional-expansion architecture (August 15–21 briefings: community-formation layer, partner-expansion layer, talent-certification layer). Tiangong Kaiwu and OpenAtom are both state-anchored open-source foundations operating in the same institutional family but with distinct institutional identities — OpenAtom operates at the national-open-source-foundation tier; Tiangong Kaiwu operates at the “Chinese-characteristic” open-source-foundation tier. From an institutional economics standpoint, this parallel-foundation architecture reveals that China’s open-source institutional ecosystem is now not a single-foundation architecture (OpenAtom only) but a multi-foundation architecture — a structurally stronger institutional-actor base with OpenAtom as the national-tier actor and Tiangong Kaiwu as the “Chinese-characteristic” framing-tier actor.
Fourth, it creates an institutional bridge to the CSDN-platform developer-acquisition mechanism. MoLe’s operational base is CSDN — the largest Chinese developer-community platform — and MoLe runs a series of developer-acquisition contests (model-quantization, domestic-compute-innovation, AI-for-X university training). By partnering with MoLe, Tiangong Kaiwu gains access to CSDN’s developer-acquisition infrastructure without building its own developer-platform. From an institutional economics standpoint, this is a governance-by-partnership move: Tiangong Kaiwu expands its institutional reach into developer-acquisition territory through a partnership-mediated access arrangement, rather than through a direct ownership arrangement. This is the same governance-by-partnership instrument documented in the OpenAtom partner-expansion layer (August 20 briefing).
Sources:
天工开物 (WeChat) — 构建中国特色AI开源协作新范式｜天工开物携手魔乐社区共建开源产业生态 天工开物 (Tiangong Kaiwu) — official portal 魔乐社区 (MoLe / Modelers) — official portal 魔乐社区 (MoLe) — developer contest roster Context: August 15–21 briefings — OpenAtom institutional-expansion architecture (three-layer: community-formation, partner-expansion, talent-certification) 🌐 ASPI (Australian Strategic Policy Institute) Deconstructs Xi’s WAIC “开源开放” Slogan as a Conceptually-Substituted Umbrella Term — A Structurally New Institutional Observation on Chinese AI Governance Discourse 3. ASPI — Alex Colville, “Some Chinese AI will go closed-source, but not all” (The Strategist, August 2026)
Alex Colville — analyst with ASPI’s Cyber, Technology and Security program — has published “Some Chinese AI will go closed-source, but not all” on The Strategist (ASPI’s policy blog) in August 2026 (aspistrategist.org.au/some-chinese-ai-will-go-closed-source-but-not-all/). The article systematically deconstructs the Chinese leadership’s use of the four-character political slogan “开源开放” (open-source-and-openness) — Xi Jinping’s headline slogan at the July 2026 World AI Conference (WAIC) in Shanghai — as a conceptually-substituted umbrella term that spans AI models, developer tools, datasets, research experience, and AI-chip architectures. Colville’s central finding: the slogan is “broad and vague enough to allow for open-source AI models to be taken off the table if required” — meaning the Chinese leadership can simultaneously endorse “open-source” and withhold frontier-model weights, without contradiction, because the slogan never referred to model weights specifically.
Per Colville: “When commentators point to Xi’s speech endorsing open-source, they should ask themselves: what does ‘open-source’ mean in a speech from the Chinese leadership? It’s important to remember that a Western concept can be imbued with different overtones when used in China. In his speech at the conference, Xi Jinping did not mention ‘open-source’ per se, but instead a four-character political slogan, ‘open source and openness’ 开源开放. That slogan first appeared in 2017 along with the first official Chinese AI policy document… and it seems to be a broad term referring to sharing any AI resources, such as research or software, that could contribute to the technology’s development.”
Colville’s article also documents the concrete evidence of the slogan’s elastic scope: ByteDance open-sources some models while keeping its flagship image and video-generation models closed-source; Alibaba’s Qwen-3.7 is proprietary (code unavailable for download) while Qwen-3.8 is pledged to be open-source; Z.ai’s Tang Jie, in a May 2025 People’s Daily op-ed, framed open-source and closed-source as “two legs” that “serve the ecosystem to develop and safeguard national security”; the July 2026 High-Level Meeting chair’s statement calls for building an “open-source ecosystem” as “an important path to the inclusive development of AI” but also stresses “respect enterprise’s independent choices” on intellectual property.
Institutional significance: This is the first documented institutional-analysis observation that deconstructs Xi Jinping’s WAIC “开源开放” slogan as a conceptually-substituted umbrella term — spanning models, tools, datasets, research experience, and chip architectures — that allows frontier-model weights to be withheld under the same slogan. From an institutional economics standpoint, this is a discourse-legitimation finding: the slogan’s elastic scope is not an accidental ambiguity but a structurally-intended instrument of Chinese AI governance discourse.
From an institutional economics perspective, ASPI’s article matters for four reasons:
First, it documents a structurally new institutional observation on the “开源开放” slogan’s elastic scope. Prior institutional-architecture cycles documented the slogan as a fixed policy object (August 16 briefing — Xi’s WAIC speech, Global Times article; August 20 briefing — “comprehensive AI governance” frame; August 23 briefing — APEC Chengdu Statement). This cycle’s ASPI documentation introduces the slogan as an elastic-institutional-instrument — a conceptually-substituted umbrella term whose elastic scope is not accidental but structurally-intended. From an institutional economics standpoint, this is a layer-reinterpretation move: the slogan has shifted from a fixed policy object to an elastic discourse instrument.
Second, it validates the “开源开放 / open-source-and-openness” concept-substitution hypothesis with a concrete institutional observation. Colville’s finding that the slogan first appeared in 2017 as a broad term — not in 2026 as a model-weights term — is the same finding documented in the August 16 and August 20 briefings’ contextual footnotes, now articulated as a frontal institutional-analysis finding by an Australian defense-think-tank analyst. From an institutional economics standpoint, this cross-institutional validation of the concept-substitution hypothesis is a structural finding with implications for how Western commentary on Chinese AI governance should process the slogan in coming cycles.
Third, it creates an institutional bridge to the Huawei CANN open-source move (item 1, this cycle) and the Tiangong Kaiwu × MoLe partnership (item 2, this cycle). Huawei’s CANN open-source move is a concrete open-compiler-institution event; Tiangong Kaiwu’s MoLe partnership is a concrete “Chinese-characteristic” partnership event. Both events operate under the same “开源开放” umbrella that ASPI’s article deconstructs. From an institutional economics standpoint, this three-source cross-institutional nexus — Huawei CANN (item 1), Tiangong Kaiwu × MoLe (item 2), ASPI’s “开源开放” deconstruction (item 3) — reveals that the elastic “开源开放” discourse-instrument is the common institutional-architecture surface on which concrete Chinese open-source institutional events now occur.
Fourth, it documents the “two legs” framing as an explicit Chinese-AI-industry discourse. Tang Jie’s May 2025 People’s Daily op-ed — “open-source and closed-source as two legs, serving the ecosystem to develop and safeguarding national security” — is the same finding documented in the August 16 and August 20 briefings’ contextual footnotes, now articulated as a frontal institutional-analysis finding by ASPI. From an institutional economics standpoint, this two-legs framing is a structural finding: the Chinese AI industry has publicly articulated that open-source and closed-source are complementary institutional instruments within a single national-interest architecture — not contradictory but paired.

China Open Source Daily — 2026-08-24 🏛️ Black Duck (Synopsys) Exits the Chinese Market — September 30 Subsidiary Closure Creates the First Documented Enterprise Compliance-Governance Vacuum in China’s Open-Source Supply Chain 1. 半导体行业观察 (Semiconductor Industry Observer), 半导体芯闻 section (August 18–19, 2026): “独家丨美国软件公司裁员，退出中国” (Exclusive: U.S. software company lays off staff, exits China)
据 半导体行业观察 独家获悉 (as documented through the WeChat article mp.weixin.qq.com/s/1i48DG-xU3thXjlOH3xJ7Q, title extracted via the WeChat article extractor, sourced through the China Daily English Input repository, 2026-08-23; corroborated by Sina Finance reprint — 突发！百达科撤离中国 — and by inf.news English translation — “A crossroads in software supply chain security”): on August 18, 2026, at an all-hands meeting, Black Duck Software — the open-source software compliance and license-governance vendor spun out of Synopsys’ Software Integrity Group in 2024 — announced it is exiting the Chinese market, closing its Chinese subsidiary 百达科软件 (Baidake), and laying off over 40 employees, with the subsidiary winding down by September 30, 2026.
Contextual background, per startupintros.com’s Black Duck profile and inf.news’s English translation: Black Duck was founded in 2002 by Doug Levin as a specialized open-source software composition analysis (SCA) and license-compliance vendor; was acquired by Synopsys in 2017 as part of its Software Integrity Group; and was carved out and rebranded back to Black Duck Software as an independent company in 2024 (per startupintros.com: “In 2017 Black Duck was acquired by Synopsys and became part of its Software Integrity Group; in 2024 that group was sold to private equity (Clearlake and Francisco Partners) and rebranded back to Black Duck Software as an independent company”). The exit therefore follows not a single-parent decision but a private-equity-owned independent company’s China-market withdrawal — a structurally distinct institutional trigger.
Institutional significance: This is the first documented exit of an enterprise-grade, Western-sourced open-source compliance and license-governance vendor from China — converting a previously-assumed-permanent institutional infrastructure (SCA / license compliance inside Chinese enterprise supply chains) into a temporal vacuum with a September 30, 2026 deadline.
From an institutional economics perspective, the Black Duck exit matters for four reasons:
First, it creates the first documented institutional-compliance-vacuum event in China’s open-source supply chain. Prior Black Duck coverage was limited to (a) the 2017 Synopsys acquisition (2017); (b) the 2024 Clearlake / Francisco Partners carve-out and rebrand (2024); (c) Synopsys’s own FY2026 2,000-job layoff tied to the $35B Ansys merger (Tech Insider, Outlook Business — a separate corporate event). This cycle’s coverage adds (d) the independent-company China-market exit — a layer-addition event that converts Black Duck from a corporate-restructuring object (prior cycles) into a market-exit object with an institutional-compliance vacuum as the downstream consequence.
Second, it creates a structurally new institutional gap in China’s open-source compliance infrastructure. Black Duck is, per inf.news’s framing, “a leading global provider of open-source software security and compliance governance” and, per CNET’s reporting (August 12, 2026), the reference enterprise-SCA vendor whose exit from China removes the only Western-sourced, enterprise-grade compliance-governance tool currently operating inside China. From an institutional economics standpoint, this compliance-vendor-exit event reveals that China’s open-source supply-chain compliance apparatus is less infrastructurally resilient than prior institutional-assumption cycles implied — the exit deadline of September 30, 2026 gives Chinese enterprise customers fewer than 45 days to relocate their SCA / license-compliance toolchain before the vendor is legally closed inside China.
Third, it creates an institutional bridge to the DeepSeek Harness / agentic-coding wave (August 19 briefing — Harness MIT release; this cycle’s item 3 — Harness pricing). Black Duck’s product domain — open-source license compliance, SCA, vulnerability analysis — is the institutional infrastructure that Chinese enterprise open-source adopters depend on for supply-chain risk management. From an institutional economics standpoint, this compliance-vacuum / agentic-coding-wave nexus reveals that China’s open-source institutional ecosystem is experiencing a compliance-layer withdrawal (Black Duck) at the same time it is experiencing an agentic-coding-layer expansion (DeepSeek Harness) — two directions on two institutional layers that do not cancel each other out but co-exist as an asymmetric institutional trajectory.
Fourth, it validates the “independent-company private-equity ownership as institutional fragility” hypothesis. The 2024 private-equity carve-out that made Black Duck an independent company — institutionally distinct from Synopsys’s prior integrated-SG ownership — is the proximate institutional precondition for the China-market exit. From an institutional economics standpoint, this PE-independent / market-exit causal-chain is a structural finding: PE-owned open-source infrastructure companies are institutionally more fragile in the China market than their prior parent-integrated counterparts were — the ownership-form change (Synopsys SG → PE-independent) is the same institutional change that made the China exit operationally possible.
Sources:

微结构eScience (WeChat, mp.weixin.qq.com/s/ipei4VrTTII0DgZqzMIzyw, title extracted via the WeChat article extractor, sourced through the China Daily English Input repository, 2026-08-23) documents that the MirrorZ 校园网联合镜像站 (Joint Mirror Station for the Academic Network) — an open-source software mirror aggregator backed by China’s CERNET (China Education and Research Network) — has been formally and publicly launched, federating the existing open-source mirror infrastructure of 27 Chinese universities plus the Chinese Academy of Sciences (中科院) into a single 302-redirect governance surface at mirrors.cernet.edu.cn / mirrors.edu.cn.
As documented through the mirrorz-org GitHub infrastructure (mirrorz-302, mirrorz-d-extension, mirrorz-help), the federation operates via a 302-redirect dispatch mechanism: MirrorZ “本身不托管文件” (does not itself host files) — instead it aggregates the existing mirror resources of the participating universities and redirects each user to the nearest / fastest / most-qualified upstream based on IP, ISP, AS, geography, and user capability flags. Per the GitHub documentation (mirrorz-302), the 302-go backend resolves user IP → CERNET/CSTNET/CHINANET/UNICOM/CMCC ISP range → best-fit endpoint (e.g., TUNA at Tsinghua, USTC mirror, SJTU mirror) — a federated-dispatch architecture in which the federation aggregates routing metadata but not data itself. Per X / landiantech (August 23, 2026, x.com/landiantech/status/2091369959419236780): “联合镜像站本身不托管文件，而是自动聚合高校现有资源为用户提供最佳镜像站。当用户实际下载时，联合镜像站将[redirect]” (The joint mirror station itself does not host files, but automatically aggregates existing university resources to provide users with the best mirror station. When a user actually downloads, the joint mirror station will redirect).
Institutional significance: This is the first documented public launch of a structurally new federated-commons governance instrument on the Chinese academic network — one in which 27 universities plus CAS federate their independently-operated mirror infrastructures into a single CERNET-governed routing surface without any single party replicating, owning, or centrally governing the data itself.
From an institutional economics perspective, MirrorZ’s launch matters for four reasons:
First, it creates a structurally new federated-commons governance instrument on CERNET. Prior Chinese open-source mirror infrastructure operated as individual university-operated sites (TUNA at Tsinghua, USTC mirror, SJTU mirror, etc.) — each governed by its own university IT or LUG community, each maintaining its own upstream sync schedule, each with its own operational continuity problem. MirrorZ’s public launch introduces a federated-dispatch governance layer — CERNET-governed routing metadata that aggregates the existing university mirrors into a single user-facing surface. From an institutional economics standpoint, this is a layer-addition event: CERNET’s federation adds a governance-layer object (302-redirect dispatch) without adding a data-layer object (central storage) — a structurally new federated-commons institutional form.
Second, it validates the “federated aggregation without centralized data” governance hypothesis with a concrete institutional observation. Prior institutional-analysis cycles documented federated-commons governance as a theoretical construct in the open-source institutional-architecture literature. MirrorZ’s launch provides the first Chinese empirical observation of federated aggregation without centralized data: the federation (CERNET / MirrorZ) controls routing; the member universities control data; no single party owns the aggregate. From an institutional economics standpoint, this routing-data separation is a structural finding with implications for how other Chinese open-source federated-commons projects (code hosting, package registries, dataset mirrors) might be governed in coming cycles.
Third, it creates an institutional bridge to the Black Duck exit (item 1, this cycle). The Black Duck exit removes the only Western-sourced, enterprise-grade open-source compliance-governance vendor inside China (item 1). MirrorZ’s launch adds a domestically-governed, CERNET-operated, federated-commons mirror infrastructure on the same timeline. From an institutional economics standpoint, this compliance-vacuum / mirror-federation nexus reveals that China’s open-source institutional ecosystem is experiencing two simultaneous institutional moves — a compliance-layer withdrawal (item 1) and a commons-layer expansion (item 2) — that do not cancel each other out but co-exist as a structurally asymmetric institutional trajectory.
Fourth, it validates the “27 universities plus CAS as parallel open-source governance actors” hypothesis. Prior open-source-actor cycles documented enterprise-led governance (Huawei, Tencent, Alibaba) and national-regulatory governance (CAICT, MIIT). MirrorZ’s federation adds a university-plus-CAS-governed commons layer — a structurally new actor form. From an institutional economics standpoint, this university-CAS parallel-actor architecture is a structural finding with implications for how China’s open-source institutional ecosystem is organized at the actor-level — not just as enterprise-led or national-regulatory but as university-CAS federated-commons in parallel.

DeepSeek / ai-Tools Review (August 13–16, 2026): “DeepSeek Harness: Open-Source Claude Code Rival” / DeepSeek V4-Pro peak/off-peak pricing effective August 16, 16:00 UTC
DeepSeek, after releasing the MIT-licensed Harness agent runtime (developer preview, August 13, 2026, documented in the August 19 briefing) and the general-availability release of V4-Pro 0813 (also August 13), moved V4-Pro from a flat per-token rate to a peak/off-peak pricing architecture effective 16:00 UTC on August 16, 2026. Institutional significance: This is the first documented monetization-architecture phase of DeepSeek’s open-weight institutional ecosystem that introduces a price-architecture move independent of the model-weights move (V4-Pro 0813) or the governance move (Harness MIT) — a structurally new phase of DeepSeek’s institutional-architecture that prior cycles did not document.
From an institutional economics perspective, the DeepSeek Harness / V4-Pro peak-off-peak pricing matters for four reasons:
First, it creates a structurally new monetization-architecture phase of DeepSeek’s open-weight institutional ecosystem. Prior DeepSeek documentation positioned DeepSeek’s institutional architecture across (a) the model-weights layer (V4 Pro MIT, April 2026 — August 16–19 briefings); (b) the agentic-infrastructure layer (Harness MIT, August 13 — August 19 briefing); (c) the corporate-governance layer (state-fund sole-vote, June 2026 — August 23 briefing); (d) the cross-sector-investment layer ($20.8M Unitree — August 21 briefing). Second, it documents the institutional pattern of “framing-as-discount / operating-as-increase” pricing strategy. Per AI Tools Review’s independent analysis: off-peak output at $1.98/M is 2.28x the old flat rate; peak output at $3.96/M is 4.55x the old flat rate. From an institutional economics standpoint, this framing-increase / discount-framing pattern is a structural finding: DeepSeek’s peak/off-peak pricing is operating as a 2.28x–4.55x price increase dressed in off-peak-discount framing — a monetization-architecture instrument with implications for how DeepSeek’s open-weight institutional ecosystem will monetize at scale.

Black Duck’s exit removes Western-sourced open-source compliance infrastructure from China; MirrorZ’s launch adds a domestically-governed federated-commons mirror infrastructure; DeepSeek Harness’s pricing move introduces a monetization-architecture phase on DeepSeek’s open-weight institutional stack.
